implementation_prompt.title: Evidence retrieval hardening: budgets, completeness reporting, clause discoverability, honest recall
implementation_prompt.base_branch: codex/backend-first-layout at 523ccd1 (Ground claims, independent override sweep, consent-first document limit)

persona.role: Retrieval hardening owner. Finish and prove the existing evidence pipeline; do not extend it. Assume every silent drop of evidence is a defect until a test proves it is reported.
persona.operating_style: One slice at a time, end to end: build, narrow checks, broad checks, independent read-only review, fix, then next slice. Smallest reversible change. Deterministic code decides budgets, exclusions and completeness. Models propose only. Never weaken a consent, tenant, privacy-gate or audit control to make a test pass.
persona.refuses: Embeddings, a vector database, new agents, a new provider, new dependencies, registry expansion, UI work, multi-policy association (separate decision), deployment.

start_here.note: Run repomap impact before editing any shared file. Check for a closer AGENTS.md in each directory changed.

confirmed_facts.fact: INVESTIGATION_LIMITS.contextBudgetBytes = 80_000 (investigate.js:11). selectContext takes the whole_policy path when total wire bytes <= budget (investigate.js:56).
STRUCTURING_GATEWAY_LIMITS.maxInputBytes = 64_000 default, env STRUCTURING_MAX_INPUT_BYTES capped at 96_000 (structuring-runtime.js:13,18).

The gateway rejects when Buffer.byteLength(contract.evidence) > maxInputBytes (model-gateway.js:79). For structuring tasks contract.evidence = JSON.stringify(payload) (prompts.js:37). The system prompt is not counted; the question, checklist, findings and JSON punctuation are.

Consequence of F1-F3: a policy whose clause wire size is between ~64 KB and 80 KB takes the whole_policy path and is rejected before the first call. This is the normal mid-size path, not an edge case.

selectSweepContext allows budgetBytes * 1.5 = 120_000 bytes (investigate.js:159), above even the 96_000 ceiling. Sweep payload also carries findings. A rejected sweep is swallowed and reported only as sweep incomplete.

policy-evidence-service.js:81 drops authorised documents beyond MAX_DOCUMENTS = 10 with no count reported. Documents failing ensureClauses with OCR_PAGES_UNAVAILABLE, OCR_PAGES_INCOMPLETE or DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND are skipped with a bare continue, also unreported.

CLAUSE_KINDS includes 'condition' and 'other' (contracts/policy-evidence.js:5). KIND_RULES has no 'condition' rule, so classifyClause never returns it; unmatched clauses become 'other' (clauses.js:8-22).

BASE_KINDS (checklist) includes 'condition' but not 'other'; SWEEP_KINDS excludes 'other', 'benefit' and 'procedure' (investigate.js:15,139). On the retrieved path a clause classified 'other' can never be selected.
recall-eval.js excludes expected clauses that cannot be located in gated text from the recall denominator (lines 17-28); the aggregate scores only resolved items.
recall-eval.js seeds the sweep with item.expected[0].quote (line 21): the golden answer is given to retrieval, which real operation never has.

assumptions.assumption: Answer contract changes stay additive (new optional fields), so stored answers stay valid. Verify validateAnswer and persistence before adding fields; if a migration is needed, stop and ask.
FTS5 search can run without a kind filter (kinds empty or omitted) through services.clauses.searchClauses. Verify in the repository before relying on it.
Clause wire size is roughly stable across gate runs, so a byte-exact payload check at call time is enough; no tokenizer is needed.

blocking_unknowns.unknown: Whether the owner prefers refusing or answering-incomplete when authorised documents exceed MAX_DOCUMENTS. Plan default: answer, force state 'conditional', report counts in unknowns and a new completeness block. Confirm before S1 BUILD.

implementation_prompt.risk_classification: data-sensitive and AI-sensitive (changes what evidence reaches Gemini and how completeness is reported). Each slice needs an independent read-only review before PR.

slice.title: Align retrieval budgets with the gateway and report every excluded document and clause
slice.outcome: No investigation payload can exceed the gateway input limit. First pass and sweep have separate budgets derived from the live gateway limit minus measured payload overhead. Every authorised document or clause not read is counted in the answer, and an incomplete read can never produce state 'evidence_found'.

owned_paths.path: src/features/ai-analysis/structuring-runtime.js (expose maxInputBytes on the call factory only; no limit change)
src/contracts/policy-evidence.js (additive completeness field, if validateAnswer requires it)
tests/policy-evidence-api.test.mjs (only if response shape assertions change)

steps.step: Make the model call factory expose its maxInputBytes (read-only). The service passes it into investigate as limits.maxInputBytes. Remove the independent 80_000 constant as the source of truth; keep it only as a fallback when no gateway limit is supplied (tests).

Add a deterministic budget function: firstPassBudget = maxInputBytes - bytes(payload without clauses) - safety margin (fixed, e.g. 2% or 1 KB, documented). sweepBudget computed the same way from the sweep payload skeleton, including the serialised findings. Both are measured with the same JSON.stringify the gateway uses (prompts.js:37).
selectContext: choose whole_policy only when the full first-pass payload fits firstPassBudget. Otherwise take the retrieved path.

selectSweepContext: replace budgetBytes * 1.5 with sweepBudget. If the first-pass context plus findings already exceeds sweepBudget, drop lowest-priority first-pass clauses not cited by any finding before adding sweep hits; never drop a cited clause. Record clauses dropped.

Before each call, assert bytes(payload) <= maxInputBytes in investigate. On violation fail with a coded INVESTIGATION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED rather than a provider error, so a regression is visible in tests.

Service: collect excluded documents with reasons: over_document_limit, ocr_unavailable, ocr_incomplete, not_found. Do not include document names or identifiers in unknowns text; counts and reasons only.

Answer: add an additive completeness block, e.g. { documentsAuthorised, documentsRead, documentsExcluded: [{reason, count}], clausesWithheldByGate, clausesNotRead, sweepClausesDropped }. Any non-zero exclusion forces state 'conditional' and adds a plain unknown line. Existing truncated and withheld handling feeds the same block.

tests.test: Policy whose payload is 1 byte under firstPassBudget: whole_policy path, gateway accepts (use the real gateway in fixture mode, not a stub).
Policy 1 byte over firstPassBudget but under 80 KB: retrieved path, gateway accepts. This test fails on current main.
Sweep near limit: many findings plus large context; sweep payload <= maxInputBytes, cited clauses kept, sweepClausesDropped reported.
STRUCTURING_MAX_INPUT_BYTES set to 96_000 and to a small value: budgets follow the setting.
12 authorised documents: 10 read, completeness reports 2 over_document_limit, state is 'conditional', unknowns mention the count.
One authorised document with OCR incomplete: reported as ocr_incomplete; answer not 'evidence_found'.
Unauthorised documents are not counted as excluded (consent filtering stays first) and never leak counts across households.
Revocation mid-run still throws CONSENT_* (no regression).

acceptance.item: No code path sends a payload above the gateway limit (asserted in tests at both limits).
Zero silent exclusions: every dropped document or clause appears in completeness.
npm run check, npm run eval:safety, npm run check:architecture, npm test, git diff --check pass.

slice.non_goals: Changing gateway default limits; token-based budgeting; chunking a policy into multiple first-pass calls.

slice.title: Make every stored clause discoverable, including 'other' and unusual conditions
slice.outcome: Clause kind is a ranking hint, not a filter. On the retrieved path and in the sweep, a relevant clause classified 'other' (or misclassified) can still reach Gemini.

owned_paths.path: src/backend/repositories (clause search only, if an unfiltered or boosted query is needed; verify path with repomap)

steps.step: Add a 'condition' rule to KIND_RULES (e.g. "subject to", "provided that", "only if", "on condition", "shall be eligible"), ordered after exclusion and waiting_period. Bump the clause builder version if clause ids or kinds are versioned so stored clauses are rebuilt; check ensureClauses behaviour first.

Retrieval order in selectContext: (a) endorsements and schedule facts, (b) an unfiltered FTS search over all kinds for the question, (c) per-kind searches as boosts interleaved by rank, (d) an explicit 'other' search. Dedup as today. Budget from S1 still caps the total.
selectSweepContext: run each sweep query once unfiltered and once with SWEEP_KINDS, and include 'other' in SWEEP_KINDS. Cap queries as today.
Keep the comment in clauses.js that kind is a retrieval aid; add that it must never gate retrieval.

tests.test: Synthetic large policy (retrieved path) whose only relevant clause is classified 'other': clause appears in first-pass context.
Same for a sweep-only override clause classified 'other' and one classified 'benefit': appears in sweep context.
classifyClause returns 'condition' for representative synthetic condition wording and does not steal exclusion or waiting-period wording.
Existing recall tests do not regress.

acceptance.item: No CLAUSE_KINDS value is unreachable by retrieval (test enumerates kinds).
Broad checks pass as in S1.

slice.title: Make the recall evaluator honest
slice.outcome: The evaluator reports end-to-end evidence recall over every expected clause, and evaluates the sweep with findings the pipeline itself produced, never with golden quotes.

owned_paths.path: scripts/ (only the existing recall runner, if one exists)

steps.step: Count unresolvable expected clauses as misses in an endToEndRecall metric (denominator = all expected). Keep retrievalRecall over resolved items as a secondary diagnostic, clearly labelled. Report unresolvable reasons separately: not_in_stored_text vs withheld_by_gate.

Remove the golden-quote seed. Two sweep modes: (a) offline: seed findings from first-pass context only, using clause subjects or titles the pipeline would see, with no expected data; (b) live: accept recorded first-pass model findings (a fixture file or a callback) so the sweep is measured against what Gemini actually returned.
Headline result = endToEndRecall for the sweep context. Report per question: expected, missed pages, unresolvable, path, and S1 completeness counts.
Fail loudly (coded RECALL_INPUT_INVALID) if golden data is passed into the sweep seed, guarded by a test.

tests.test: Golden item with one unresolvable expected clause: endToEndRecall < 1 while retrievalRecall can be 1.
Sweep seed contains no text from expected quotes (assert by substring check).
Recorded-findings mode produces the same sweep context as investigate given the same findings.

acceptance.item: Synthetic tests only. The report states that recall on real policies is unmeasured until the owner runs it on a human-verified corpus.
Broad checks pass as in S1.

slice.non_goals: Building the human-verified corpus; committing any real policy text or golden quotes from real policies.

after_slices.item: Run the corrected evaluator on a human-verified policy corpus kept outside the repository; record only aggregate numbers in LATEST.md.
Run one complete live backend journey (upload, Sarvam OCR, clauses, question, Gemini first pass and sweep) and verify citations, exclusions and omissions by hand.
Decide multi-policy association (issue 5) separately; until then multi-document answers keep the existing warning and the S1 completeness block.

verification.rule: Mocked or fixture-mode tests do not prove the live journey. Each slice report states what remains unverified.
Independent read-only review per slice (AI and data-sensitive change) before PR.

implementation_prompt.rollback: Each slice is one PR with no migration (stop and ask if one becomes necessary). Revert the PR to roll back. S2 may change stored clause kinds through a builder version bump; rollback means clauses rebuild under the old version on next ensureClauses.
implementation_prompt.report_format: Per slice: changes with file:line, tests added, check results, unverified items, security and data impact, rollback, follow-ups. Update docs/iterations/LATEST.md only when a slice merges.
